research_question: Do the E080 Borda and E081 minimum-component-rank aggregators provide meaningfully distinct candidate orderings from the existing mean-z consensus, or do they mostly reshuffle the same candidate information?
novelty_statement: E080 and E081 measured candidate recall and portfolio outcomes but did not report the full per-target 45-number rank-correlation matrix or top-K set-overlap geometry across all three rankers. This study measures rank dependence and unique winner rescue without changing any model, feature, coefficient, candidate threshold, or allocator.

prior_work_boundary.E080: Borda candidate recall and fixed three-line allocator outcomes; this study adds rank-dependence and overlap metrics only.
prior_work_boundary.E081: MIN_RANK candidate recall, fixed three-line allocator outcomes, and best-component miss attribution; this study adds full-ranking dependence and pairwise top-K overlap only.
prior_work_boundary.E059_E065: Component-level candidate recall diagnostics; no component or aggregation is reweighted here.
prior_work_boundary.duplication_control: No new model variant, feature, parameter search, allocator experiment, or post-result tuning is permitted.

source.provenance: repository snapshot; SHA-256 correction and Git blob identity were audited on 2026-11-23; secondary cross-check only, direct official API not retrieved

models.CONSENSUS: Mean of the five existing component z-scores; descending score, then ascending number.
models.BORDA: Sum of the five existing component rank positions; ascending sum, then ascending number.
models.MIN_RANK: Ascending minimum of the five component rank positions; tie-break by ascending sum of component ranks, then ascending number.

features.definitions: Exact automation/candidate_recall_v1.py features: population z-scores; recent30 count over prior 30 draws; gap in completed draws since last main-number appearance; momentum=(last10/10)-(preceding20/20), with exact integer rank score 2*last10-preceding20; balanced=(recent30_z+gap_z)/2; contrarian=(-recent30_z+gap_z)/2.
features.cutoff_rule: For every target t, all five component features and all three model rankings use only draws 1..t-1. Target outcomes are read only after all rankings for t are frozen.

primary_metrics.full_ranking_dependence: Per-target Spearman rank correlation over all 45 numbers for each of the three model pairs; summarize mean, median, and 10th/90th percentiles.
primary_metrics.top_k_overlap: For K in [10,15,20,25,30], per-target intersection size and Jaccard similarity for each model pair; summarize mean and block ranges.
primary_metrics.exact_overlap_reference: For two independent uniform K-subsets of 45 numbers, expected intersection is K*K/45. This is a descriptive independent-random reference, not a model performance gate.
primary_metrics.unique_winner_rescue: At each K, count winners captured by model A but not B and vice versa; summarize per-target means and total counts. This is descriptive only.
primary_metrics.candidate_recall: Report each ranker's recall@K as a supporting descriptive metric; no separate promotion test.

stability.partition: Targets 401..1250 as 17 consecutive non-overlapping 50-target blocks; target 1251 retained and reported as a separate 1-target remainder.
stability.report: Per-pair Spearman and top-K overlap block means/ranges; per-pair unique-winner-rescue differences by block. Do not discard the remainder.

inference_and_decision.purpose: Diagnose redundancy or distinctness among existing candidate rankers and guide whether future work should focus on candidate information or allocator geometry.

guardrails: No future leakage; target t uses only rounds through t-1.
No new candidate list, TOP30, core/tail list, purchase lines, or fallback.
No change to the fixed strict gate or prospective minimum-count policy.
No model or allocator promotion from this diagnostic.
